subject: Operator classification, telemetry escrow ask, and subprocessor notice timeline
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@brightcare.com>

Cc: J. Lopez <jlopez@hartleylegal.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jul 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood DPA/addendum questions re: telemetry & operator carveouts

Hi Connor —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we start legal intake for a pilot contract, our privacy team raised a few questions in the attached draft addendum (BrightCare-Redwood-Privacy-Addendum_v1.docx). High-level asks:

- We need clarity whether Redwood will accept an "operator" designation (vs. "service provider") for CCPA/CPRA language where applicable. BrightCare wants the limited-use protections preserved, but we also need guarantees for telemetry used for product analytics that are not tied to customer PII.
- For telemetry and aggregated analytics: can Redwood commit to an escrowed audit path or onshore fallback if an external analytics subprocessor is used? Our security policy prefers an explicit onshore fallback for US-state regulated data.
- Subprocessor notice and emergency onboarding: can you confirm the timeline (notice / approval / emergency activation) and what evidence you can provide (SOC 2 scope, encryption proofs, dataflow diagrams)?

Can you loop in your privacy/legal SME and let us know the earliest we can get a redline? We are targeting an initial pilot SOW in late July, so a decision this month would be ideal.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Privacy & Compliance
BrightCare Health

Samira — appreciate the clear list. Looping in Marissa (privacy counsel) and Karthik (solutions) to confirm technical constraints and legal posture. A couple of quick notes so you have context while Marissa reviews:

- We routinely classify customers as "service provider" under CCPA/CPRA where customers request that mapping, but Redwood also supports a limited set of "operator" behaviors when the customer has explicit contractual controls and onshore fallback requirements.
- For telemetry, we separate PII-based request traces from aggregated metrics; many customers want aggregated analytics retained for product improvement and SLOs. We can discuss protections and onshore fallback in more detail.

Marissa — can you confirm whether we can accept BrightCare's proposed operator carveout for analytics, and whether an escrow/audit path is feasible? Karthik — can you summarize typical subprocessor notice timelines and what evidence we can provide by EOW?

Will aim to get a redline by Wed Jul 9 EOD if possible. If not, we'll propose a short call.

Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 09:11:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA/addendum questions re: telemetry & operator carveouts

Hi Samira — thanks, reviewed the draft and provided inline guidance below. I attached a short redline (BC-Redline-v2.docx) and pasted the key suggested language for quick review.

Quick answers:
1) Operator vs Service Provider
- We can accept an "operator" designation for narrowly-scoped telemetry processing that BrightCare explicitly defines as non-personal and aggregated, provided: (a) BrightCare defines the data fields and retention; (b) Redwood is permitted to use aggregated telemetry only for platform operations and product improvement (no re-identification); and (c) there is an onshore fallback described in section 5.
- Suggested clause (short): "For telemetry explicitly defined in Appendix A (aggregated, non-identifiable metrics), the parties agree Redwood shall be treated as an Operator solely for the limited purpose of operating and improving Redwood services. Such Operator status does not expand Redwood's rights to use or disclose Customer Personal Information beyond the limited telemetry scope."

2) Telemetry escrow / onshore fallback
- We do not typically escrow telemetry to third parties, but we can commit to: (a) an onshore fallback path where telemetry that would otherwise go to an overseas analytics vendor is routed to a US-based subprocessor in the event of export restrictions or an incident; (b) 72-hour activation SLA for emergency onboarding of an onshore fallback subprocessor; and (c) evidence (subprocessor runbooks and encryption at-rest/in-transit proofs) within 5 business days of request.
- Suggested clause (short): "Redwood will maintain an onshore fallback plan for telemetry processing and will make available runbook summary and encryption attestations within five (5) business days upon Customer request. Emergency activation of the onshore fallback subprocessor will be completed within seventy-two (72) hours of mutual agreement that activation is necessary."

3) Subprocessor notice & emergency onboarding timelines
- Standard notice for new subprocessors is 30 days; we provide a written notice email and an opt-out window only for subprocessors that pose elevated risk per the Customer's reasonable security review. For emergencies (e.g., urgent failover or legal requirement), we can do a 72-hour onboarding with written confirmation and post-facto notice.
- We can provide SOC 2 report access under NDA and dataflow diagrams scoped to the services BrightCare will use. We cannot provide raw telemetry logs without a lawful basis.

4) Evidence & proofs
- What we can provide quickly: SOC 2 Type II summary, encryption at-rest/in-transit statement, subprocessor list, basic dataflow diagrams, and retention mappings. For deeper forensics or source logs we'd need a DSAR/legal process.

Next steps I propose:
- I uploaded a redline (BC-Redline-v2.docx) with tracked changes addressing the operator language + proposed SLA windows.
- If BrightCare is okay with the 72-hour emergency onboarding and 5-business-day evidence window, I can sign off and we can hand to your counsel for a quick final review.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk through the redlines (Marissa, Karthik, Connor) with Samira + J. Lopez.

Regards,

Marissa — really helpful, thank you. The proposed 72-hour emergency onboarding and 5 business day evidence window are reasonable. A few clarifying items before we proceed to a final sign-off:

- Please confirm Appendix A will be editable by BrightCare and that any future additions to Appendix A (new telemetry fields) require mutual written agreement.
- We need the runbook summary to include the onshore vendor name (can be redacted for procurement reasons until contract execution) and a brief escalation path (phone/email).
- Can you confirm retention max for aggregated telemetry (we'd prefer 18 months default unless a customer specifies otherwise)?

If you can accept the above, J. Lopez and I are happy to take the redline. Would you have availability for a 30-min call tomorrow morning (Thu 10 Jul) 10:00-10:30am PT? Otherwise we can finalize by email. I dropped the redline back with two small edits to Appendix A and included our DocuSign link here: https://docu.sign/abc123-redwood-addendum

Thanks again — this is moving fast in a good way.
